dct_description_sm: In this two-year project (2013-2015), we will conduct a harvest monitoring study of trace metal bioaccumulation in local country foods at Kuujjuaraapik in Nunavik. The Sakkuq Landholding Corporation of Kuujjuaraapik is interested in obtaining information on metal concentrations in locally harvested foods, for which recent information is not available. Twenty years ago, extensive measurements were taken of metal concentrations in aquatic and terrestrial wildlife near Kuujjuaraapik as part of a major environmental assessment for the Great Whale hydro-electric project. In addition to updating information on local country foods, the old measurements provide an opportunity to determine if levels have changed in the last two decades.  The specific objectives are to: (1) Collect locally harvested foods near Kuujjuaraapik for metals analysis, during the winter and summer seasons, and in both aquatic and terrestrial environments; (2) Collect ancillary measurements on the harvested animals where feasible (e.g., size, location of capture, ageing structures); (3) Measure concentrations of metals (including mercury, lead, cadmium) in relevant tissues (e.g., muscle, liver); and (4) Determine if metal concentrations in terrestrial and aquatic animals have changed since previous measurements were conducted 20 years ago.
dct_subject_sm: Social sciences, economics and policy -> Environmental health
dct_title_s: Harvest monitoring of metal bioaccumulation at Kuujjuaraapik (Nunavik): Have levels changed 20 years after the Great Whale environmental assessment?
